Two-step verification: test guide

How to check, on the live site, that sign-up and two-step verification (MFA) work from start to finish. About 15 minutes. You need your phone with Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator, and a fresh email address.

I ran this whole journey first on our local copy (same site and sign-in code as live, a local database, the sign-in service simulated) with a test person, "Priya Sharma". These are its screenshots; your screens will match. The WorkOS sign-in page in step 13 is the real one. Step 14, where WorkOS asks for the authenticator code, has no screenshot: only a real sign-in can show it, and that is your test.

A. Sign upB. Turn on two-stepC. Sign out / sign inD. Extra checksChecklist

A. Create a new account (the one-page sign-up)

1

Open the site, signed out

Go to attackedmap.vercel.app in a private window (or sign out first). Click Sign up free on the welcome box (or any gold sign-up button).

You should seeThe home page with its welcome box. Every sign-up button opens the sign-up page.

2

The sign-up page

You can also open it directly: attackedmap.vercel.app/?signup.

You should seeEvery question on one page: first name, surname, email, job title, company, industry.

3

Fill everything in, then Continue

Use a fresh address so it counts as a new user, e.g. yourname+mfa1@gmail.com (it arrives in your normal inbox). Pick a job title and an industry, type a company, then press Continue.

You should seeThe button changes to "Sending your code…".

4

Type the code from the email

Open the email from Attacked.ai / WorkOS and type the 6-digit code. Check there is only ONE email.

You should see"Check your email", the address you typed, a code box, and Resend (after 30 s).

5

Your dashboard

Press Create account.

You should seeYour industry's dashboard straight away. No "One last step" box. A small card offers two-step verification ("Set it up" / "Remind me later") — it is optional.

B. Turn on two-step verification

6

Open Login and security

Click your initial (top right) → Login and security. (Or press "Set it up" on the card.)

You should seeThe account menu with "Login and security".

7

Login and security

Scroll down to Two-step verification.

You should seeYour sign-in email, password, linked accounts, last sign-in and signed-in devices; then Two-step verification OFF with two options: Passkey and Authenticator app.

8

Authenticator app → Set up

Install Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator on your phone. Press Set up under Authenticator app and scan the QR code with the app (or type the key by hand).

You should seeA QR code, a key you can copy, and a box for the code.

9

Type the app's code, then Confirm

Type the 6-digit code your app shows for Attacked.ai and press Confirm.

You should seeThe Confirm button lights up once six digits are in.

10

Two-step is On

—

You should seeAuthenticator app ON, "On since today", and a green line: next time you sign in, the sign-in page will ask for a code from your app.

11

The confirmation email

Check your inbox.

You should seeAn email: "Two-step verification turned on for your Attacked.ai account".

C. Sign out and sign in again — THE MAIN TEST

12

Sign out

Initial (top right) → Sign out. Then click Sign in (top right).

You should seeThe home page, signed out.

13

The WorkOS sign-in page

Sign in the way you like: email code (type the address, then the emailed code), or Google / Microsoft if that address is a Google / Microsoft account.

You should seeThe Attacked.ai sign-in page (hosted by WorkOS). This screenshot is the real page.

14

WorkOS asks for the authenticator code

This is the check your senior asked about. After the email code (or Google / Microsoft), WorkOS should ask: enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app. Open the app, type the current code.

You should seeA code box on the WorkOS page. Take a screenshot of it and send it to me. If WorkOS does not ask for the code and lets you straight in, tell me: that is the one thing still unproven.

No screenshot for this screen. It belongs to WorkOS and only appears after a real sign-in with two-step on, which I am not allowed to do on the live system. You will be the first to see it.
15

Back on your dashboard

—

You should seeYour dashboard, signed in.

D. Extra checks

16

The sign-up page never skips the code

Sign out. Open /?signup and fill it in with the same address (the one with two-step on), then type the emailed code.

You should see"This address already has an account with two-step verification, so it signs in on the secure sign-in page. Taking you there…" — then the WorkOS page, which asks for the authenticator code.

17

Turn two-step off

Login and security → Authenticator app → Turn off, type a current code from the app, press Turn off two-step.

You should seeIt asks for a current code first (and a recent sign-in). An email confirms it.

18

Two-step is Off again

—

You should seeAuthenticator app back to Set up. The next sign-in asks for the email code only.

19

On a phone

Repeat steps 6–10 on your phone if you like.

You should seeThe same cards, one under the other.
